findings.title: Minimum token schema uses computed string keys, not a real schema for expiry
findings.body: The keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` are computed property names evaluating to the literal string "ZodString"/"ZodOptional" etc. The schema therefore does not validate any expiry field and the 'any property with a number is the expiry' intent is not implemented. Under sync mode, refreshed tokens are accepted without checking expiry_date/expires_in, and callers that rely on expiry (e.g. Google, Zoom) can store undefined expiry, causing tokens to be treated as expired or never refreshed.

findings.title: Fallback sets refresh_token to the literal string 'refresh_token'
findings.body: When the response has no refresh_token, the function writes the placeholder string "refresh_token" into the parsed data. That value is then persisted to the credential, overwriting the real refresh token with a garbage value, so future refreshes against the provider fail.

findings.title: Sync endpoint fetch has no error handling and no auth header
findings.body: The fetch to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT sends the user id and app slug without any authentication, and the response is returned unchecked. A non-2xx response or HTML error page is returned as if it were a token response; callers like Google (`res?.data`) and Hubspot then treat it as valid tokens. Also the refresh path for user credentials is entirely bypassed when sync is on, so a failure in the sync endpoint silently breaks refresh with no fallback.

findings.title: Webhook secret compared with non-constant-time equality and undefined-safe
findings.body: The header is compared with `!==` against process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET. If the env var is unset, the header is undefined on requests without it and undefined === undefined passes, but the code path is guarded only by APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED. Also the comparison is not timing-safe. Use crypto.timingSafeEqual and explicitly reject when the secret is empty.

findings.title: Decryption and JSON.parse errors are unhandled and produce 500s; invalid input is not validated
findings.body: symmetricDecrypt and JSON.parse on reqBody.keys are not wrapped in try/catch, and appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse throws a ZodError rather than returning a 400. Malformed or wrongly encrypted payloads cause unhandled exceptions. Also an empty CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY is passed as '' rather than rejected.

findings.title: App lookup and metadata lookup are redundant and the credential is matched on the wrong field
findings.body: The code looks up the app by slug, then looks up appStoreMetadata by app.slug and uses appMetadata.slug for the credential appId. The DB app row is only used for existence. Credential matching by userId+appId via findFirst also does not restrict type, so an existing credential of a different type for the same app would be overwritten with new keys. Creation sets type from metadata but updates never reconcile type.

findings.title: prisma is used but never imported in CalendarService
findings.body: getClient now calls prisma.credential.update, but the file imports no prisma client (the import list has no `prisma`). This is a compile/runtime ReferenceError when a Salesforce credential is used.

findings.title: Salesforce token refresh now always hits the network and ignores the stored token and the sync path
findings.body: getClient unconditionally POSTs to login.salesforce.com on every service construction, with no expiry check, and no sync-endpoint branch via refreshOAuthTokens, unlike other apps. This changes behavior for every Salesforce calendar operation (extra latency and requests per call), and self-hosters using sync will still hit Salesforce directly. The response.statusText !== 'OK' check is also fragile since HTTP/2 responses may have empty statusText, causing false failures.

findings.title: Refreshed Salesforce key drops fields and writes parsed data that excludes instance_url
findings.body: The persisted key is `{...accessTokenParsed.data, refresh_token}` but salesforceTokenSchema parses only listed fields, and zod strips unknown keys. Salesforce's refresh response includes instance_url, and it is in the schema, so that holds, but other stored fields like the original `expiry` info are lost; additionally the connection now uses credentialKey.instance_url (old) rather than the refreshed one.

findings.title: Removed error logging and tokenResponse.success check changes failure behavior
findings.body: The zod-failure console.error was removed, and parseRefreshTokenResponse now throws on invalid responses instead of returning a failed result. The code then still spreads `tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data`, which is dead logic since the function either throws or returns a successful result. Errors from Microsoft (e.g. invalid_grant) now surface as an unhelpful error instead of being logged with the MS response.

findings.title: Zoom refresh computes expiry from expires_in which is absent in sync mode
findings.body: After parseRefreshTokenResponse, key.expiry_date is set from newTokens.expires_in * 1000. In sync mode the minimum schema does not require expires_in, so expires_in can be undefined, producing NaN expiry_date and a token that is never considered expired or always considered expired depending on comparison.

findings.title: Webex expiry only updated when expires_in present, leaving stale expiry_date
findings.body: The refreshed token only updates expiry_date if expires_in is present, and the refresh path is now reachable through sync which may omit expires_in. The stored expiry_date then stays in the past, causing a refresh on every call.

findings.title: APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is a string or undefined, not a boolean
findings.body: The expression evaluates to the env string (or undefined), not a boolean. It is used in `if` checks and returned in the webhook gate, which works by truthiness but the exported type is misleading and an empty-string secret is treated as disabled while whitespace is enabled. Should be wrapped in Boolean().

findings.title: Zoho CRM expiry is hardcoded to one hour regardless of response
findings.body: zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.expiryDate is set to Date.now()+60*60 (missing *1000 is fine but expires_in is ignored), which is an existing pattern but now also runs for sync-supplied tokens whose lifetime may differ, so tokens can be treated as valid after expiry.

findings.title: Zoho CRM callback expiryDate adds 3600 ms instead of seconds
findings.body: Math.round(Date.now() + 60 * 60) adds only 3.6 seconds, not one hour, so the stored expiryDate is effectively now and tokens are immediately treated as expired.

findings.title: Redirect URI hardcoded to zoho-bigin, changing the slug-based value
findings.body: The redirect URI was changed from using appConfig.slug to a literal string. This is harmless now but removes the single source of truth and must match callback.ts, which still uses appConfig.slug; any future slug change will break the OAuth redirect mismatch.

findings.title: CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME added to globalEnv out of alphabetical order and duplicates exist
findings.body: The new env vars are inserted out of order, and INTERCOM_SECRET was already duplicated in the list. Minor, but the list is clearly maintained sorted and this makes future diffs noisier.

findings.title: CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME comment says lowercase but code reads it directly from req.headers
findings.body: Node lowercases incoming header names, so the code works only if the env value is lowercase. The comment states the requirement but the code does not normalize it, so a mixed-case value silently fails with 403 for every request.

findings.title: No tests cover the new sync path or the parse fallback behavior
findings.body: The PR adds a new sync mode affecting ~15 apps, a new webhook endpoint, and parse fallback logic, but the PR checklist states no tests were added. Bugs such as the broken zod schema and the 'refresh_token' placeholder would have been caught by unit tests.
